label: Inactive holy site faiths
summary: The list of inactive faiths that the holy site window shows for this holy site.
details: Vanilla shows the list's size in the header 'Holy Site for inactive faiths (n)' and fills a list in the holy site window with it. The list is hidden when it is empty. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Remove button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the remove button in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla puts it directly into a tooltip line of the holy site window GUI.

label: Remove artifact tooltip
summary: Text describing what removing the given artifact from the holy site would do.
details: Vanilla passes `Artifact.Self` (the artifact of the current list row) and shows the result as a text in the holy site window. Going by its name and that one use, the text belongs to removing an artifact.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact the text is about.

label: Selected action effect text
summary: A text describing the effect of the action currently chosen in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the holy site window. Going by its name, the action is the one picked in that window; which actions exist is not shown in the input.

label: Selected artifact
summary: The artifact currently selected in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla only asks it whether it is valid (`.IsValid`), which tells whether anything is selected, and shows or hides parts of the window with that. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Selected slot
summary: The slot currently selected in the holy site window.
details: Going by its name, it gives the chosen artifact slot of the holy site. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on the inventory and royal court windows is used to read a slot's name or as a data context, which is only a hint.

label: Holy site slots
summary: The list of artifact slots of the holy site.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list in the holy site window, so the window shows one entry per slot. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Sorted artifacts
summary: The list of artifacts in the holy site window, in the chosen sort order.
details: Going by its name, it gives artifacts already sorted. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The inventory window uses the same name as the source of its artifact list, which is only a hint.

label: Has selected filled slot
summary: Whether the selected slot of the holy site already holds an artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its opposite with `Not`, to switch between two primary buttons of the holy site window: one labelled swap (shown when it is true) and one labelled enshrine (shown otherwise). That a filled slot means an artifact sits in it is read from the name.

label: Has selected slot
summary: Whether a slot is selected in the holy site window.
details: Going by its name, it is true once a slot has been chosen. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The inventory window uses the same name to disable a button while no slot is selected, which is only a hint.

label: Abandon button visible
summary: Whether the abandon button is shown in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the visibility of the button for the 'abandon holy site' decision, which is placed in the holy site window.

label: Adopt button visible
summary: Whether the adopt button is shown in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the visibility of the button for the 'adopt holy site' decision, which is placed in the holy site window.

label: Is artifact selected
summary: Whether the given artifact is the one selected in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla passes `Artifact.Self` (the artifact of the current list row) and uses the result for a button's pressed state, sometimes together with `IsSelectedSlot`, so the row looks pushed in while selected.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to check.

label: Artifact sort descending
summary: Whether the artifact list is sorted in descending order.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. The inventory and royal court windows use the same name to choose the frame of the sort order button, which is only a hint.

label: Demote button visible
summary: Whether the demote button is shown in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the visibility of the button for the 'demote holy site' decision, which is placed in the holy site window.

label: Elevate button visible
summary: Whether the elevate button is shown in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla uses it to set the visibility of the button for the 'elevate holy site' decision, which is placed in the holy site window.

label: Enshrine button enabled
summary: Whether the enshrine button can be clicked in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the enabled state of the swap button and the enshrine button; both run `OnEnshrineButtonClicked` when clicked.

label: Remove button enabled
summary: Whether the remove button can be clicked in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the enabled state of the remove button of the holy site window, whose tooltip comes from `GetRemoveButtonTooltip` and whose click runs `OnRemoveButtonClicked`.

label: Selected artifact enshrined
summary: Whether the selected artifact is already enshrined.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it anywhere, so nothing confirms what exactly it checks.

label: Is selected slot
summary: Whether the given slot is the one selected in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla passes `InventorySlot.Self` (the slot of the current list row) and uses the result to show or hide parts of a row and to choose the text of the slot's tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The slot to check.

label: Enshrine button click
summary: Reacts to a click on the enshrine button in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click handler of two buttons. It returns nothing. Going by its name, it carries out the enshrining.

label: Remove button click
summary: Reacts to a click on the remove button in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click handler of one button. It returns nothing. The text on that button is the remove-artifact button label; what the click does beyond that is read from the name only.

label: Select artifact
summary: Makes the given artifact the selected one in the holy site window.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click and passes `Artifact.Self`, the artifact of the clicked list row. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to select.

label: The window itself
summary: The holy site window object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the window on, for example as an argument to another function. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Sort artifacts
summary: Sorts the artifact list of the holy site window.
details: Going by its name, it sorts by the chosen order. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The inventory and royal court windows call the same name when a sort selection changes, which is only a hint. It returns nothing and takes one value.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A value the game does not describe; likely the sort choice.

label: Toggle artifact sort order
summary: Switches the artifact list between ascending and descending order.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The inventory and royal court windows call the same name from a click, which is only a hint. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle selected slot
summary: Selects the given slot in the holy site window, or clears the selection if it was already selected.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click and passes `InventorySlot.Self`, the slot of the clicked row. The select-or-clear behaviour is taken from the word Toggle in the name. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The slot to toggle.

label: Unequip artifact
summary: Takes the given artifact out of its slot in the holy site window.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it anywhere. It returns nothing and takes one value, probably the artifact.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A value the game does not describe; likely the artifact.

label: Hook itself (access)
summary: The hook object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on a hook. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Expiration date
summary: The date on which the hook expires.
details: Vanilla asks it for `.GetString` to write 'Expires <date>' in the intrigue window. Only some hooks have such a date; see `HasExpirationDate`.

label: Hook icon frame
summary: A whole number that picks the frame of the hook's icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as the frame number of an image in the intrigue window. What each number looks like is not shown in the input.

label: Hook strength
summary: A text naming how strong the hook is.
details: Vanilla puts it into the intrigue window's text about the hook's strength.

label: Hook name
summary: The name of the hook as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the intrigue window. The same function name is used a very large number of times on other types.

label: Has expiration date
summary: Whether the hook expires on a certain date.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the expiry line in the intrigue window only for hooks that have one.

label: The hook itself
summary: The hook object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the hook on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on a hook. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Window itself (access)
summary: The hostage exchange window object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Can clear
summary: Whether the chosen hostages can be cleared in the hostage exchange window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the enabled state of a button in the war overview window. It is paired with `OnClear`.

label: Can exchange hostage
summary: Whether a hostage exchange is possible right now.
details: Vanilla uses it both to show a part of the war overview window and to enable a control in it.

label: Can send
summary: Whether the hostage proposal can be sent.
details: Vanilla uses it for the enabled state of a button in the war overview window. It is paired with `Send`.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the hostage exchange window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click in the war overview GUI. It returns nothing. Other windows have a function of the same name.

label: Acceptance breakdown tooltip
summary: The tooltip text explaining how willing the other side is to accept the given character as a hostage.
details: Vanilla passes `CharacterListItem.Self`, the character of the current list row, and shows the result as a tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list entry of the character the tooltip is about.
fields.values: a character list item, e.g. CharacterListItem.Self

label: Action info text
summary: A text describing the hostage action being prepared.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the war overview window. Its exact wording is not shown in the input.

label: Actor
summary: The character who acts in the hostage exchange.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the window and compares it to `GetRecipient`; parts are only shown when the two are different characters. Going by the names, the actor is the one starting the exchange. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Character list
summary: The list of characters shown for choosing a hostage.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of lists in the war overview window. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Demanded character
summary: The character chosen to be demanded as a hostage.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the war overview window. The game documents no return type for it. See also `HasSelectedDemandCharacter`.

label: Header text
summary: The header text of the hostage exchange window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the war overview window.

label: Hostage acceptance value
summary: A number for how willing the other side is to accept the given hostage.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it anywhere. It takes one value, probably the character, and returns a fixed-point number.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A value the game does not describe; likely the hostage.

label: Left label
summary: The label text for the left side of the hostage exchange window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the war overview window. See also `GetLabelRight`.

label: Right label
summary: The label text for the right side of the hostage exchange window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the war overview window. See also `GetLabelLeft`.

label: Offered character
summary: The character chosen to be offered as a hostage.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the war overview window. The game documents no return type for it. See also `HasSelectedOfferCharacter`.

label: Recipient
summary: The character who receives the hostage proposal.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the window, asks it whether it is the player, and compares it to `GetActor`. Going by the names, the recipient is the other side of the exchange. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Secondary actor
summary: The secondary actor of the hostage exchange window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the war overview window. Who this character is, and how they differ from the actor, is not shown in the input.

label: Has demanded character
summary: Whether a character has been chosen to be demanded as a hostage.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its opposite with `Not`, to switch between two parts of the war overview window.

label: Has offered character
summary: Whether a character has been chosen to be offered as a hostage.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its opposite with `Not`, to switch between two parts of the war overview window.

label: Is open
summary: Whether the hostage exchange window is open.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the war overview window only while the exchange is open.

label: Clear click
summary: Clears the hostage choices when the clear button is clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click. It returns nothing. See `CanClear` for when the button is enabled. That it clears the choices is read from the name.

label: Open demand hostage
summary: Opens the choice of which hostage to demand.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of three controls in the war overview window. It returns nothing. The result is read from the name.

label: Open offer hostage
summary: Opens the choice of which hostage to offer.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of three controls in the war overview window. It returns nothing. The result is read from the name.

label: The window itself
summary: The hostage exchange window object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the window on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Send proposal
summary: Sends the hostage proposal.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the war overview window. It returns nothing. See `CanSend` for when the button is enabled.

label: Would accept hostage
summary: Whether the other side might accept the given character as a hostage.
details: Vanilla passes `CharacterListItem.Self`, the character of the current list row, and uses the result and its opposite to show or hide row parts. The word potentially in the name suggests a rough check, not a final answer.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The list entry of the character to check.
fields.values: a character list item, e.g. CharacterListItem.Self

label: Aspiration itself (access)
summary: The house aspiration object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Change effect text
summary: The text describing what changing the house to this aspiration does.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the confirm button while the change is allowed; otherwise it shows the reason the command is not possible.

label: Upgrade effect text
summary: The text describing what upgrading this aspiration does.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the upgrade button while the upgrade is allowed; otherwise it shows the reason the command is not possible.

label: Icon
summary: The icon image of the house aspiration.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of images on the map icon layer, in the dynasty house window and in the house aspiration window. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Illustration
summary: The large illustration image of the house aspiration.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an image in the house aspiration window. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Level AI score
summary: A number showing how much the AI values the given level of this aspiration for the given character.
details: Vanilla prints it as 'AI score' in the house aspiration window, passing `GetPlayer` and the index of the level row. What the first value stands for is taken from that use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the score is for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The index of the level.

label: Level description
summary: The description text of one level of the aspiration.
details: Vanilla uses it in the texts for setting or upgrading an aspiration and in the house power level tooltip. It takes two values; vanilla's lines in the input are cut off, so what exactly they are is not shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A value the game does not describe; likely the level index.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A value the game does not describe.

label: Level name
summary: The name of one level of the aspiration.
details: Vanilla passes a level index, for example the house's current level index or the index of a list row, and puts the name into tooltips and headings.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The index of the level.

label: Levels
summary: The list of levels of the house aspiration.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of lists in the admin vassal detail window and the dynasty house window. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Name
summary: The name of the house aspiration as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the family attribute window and in texts about setting or changing an aspiration. The same function name is used a very large number of times on other types.

label: Small icon
summary: The small icon image of the house aspiration.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of images in the admin vassal detail window and the family attribute window. See `HasSmallIcon`. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the house aspiration has an icon.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use the same name to show an icon only when there is one, which is only a hint.

label: Has multiple levels
summary: Whether the house aspiration has more than one level.
details: Vanilla uses it to show level parts of the admin vassal detail window and the house aspiration window, and to add a level note to a tooltip heading.

label: Has small icon
summary: Whether the house aspiration has a small icon.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it anywhere.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether there is a real house aspiration here, not an empty one.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of a window only when an aspiration exists, and to choose between showing its name or something else in a text. The same name is used on very many types.

label: The aspiration itself
summary: The house aspiration object itself.
details: Vanilla passes it to other functions: to select an aspiration on a click, and to compare it with the window's current aspiration or with the 'no_aspect' aspiration.

label: Level itself (access)
summary: The house aspiration level object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: The level itself
summary: The house aspiration level object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the level on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Window itself (access)
summary: The house aspiration window object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Can edit
summary: Whether the player may change the house aspiration in this window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show editing parts of the house aspiration window.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the house aspiration window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of three controls in the window. It returns nothing. Other windows have a function of the same name.

label: Confirm aspiration
summary: The command that sets the house to the chosen aspiration.
details: Vanilla checks it with `IsValidCommand` for the enabled state of a button, opens a confirmation popup with `CreateCommandPopup` on click, and shows the reason in the tooltip when it is not valid. It is a command, not a plain function.

label: Available aspirations
summary: The list of house aspirations the player can choose from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of lists in the window, and checks its size (six or more) to decide on a layout. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Dynasty house
summary: The dynasty house the window is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window and asks it for its current aspiration. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Selected aspiration
summary: The house aspiration currently chosen in the window.
details: Vanilla compares it with each aspiration of the list to mark the chosen one as pressed or visible. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Level icon
summary: The icon image for the given level of the aspiration.
details: Vanilla passes the index of the level row and uses the result as an image texture. The game documents no return type for it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The index of the level.

label: Aspiration cooldown
summary: A text with the time before the house aspiration can be changed again.
details: Vanilla puts it into the warning 'You cannot change ... for the next ...' in the family attribute window.

label: Aspiration cost text
summary: A text describing what the chosen house aspiration costs.
details: Vanilla puts it into the line 'Cost: ...' in the family attribute window. See `HasSelectedHouseAspirationCost`.

label: Selected level
summary: The aspiration level currently selected in the window.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it anywhere. The window works with a selected level index instead; see `IsSelectedLevelIndex`.

label: Has aspiration cost
summary: Whether the chosen house aspiration has a cost.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the cost parts of the window only when there is a cost.

label: Current aspiration selected
summary: Whether the aspiration the house already has is the one chosen in the window.
details: Going by its name for the meaning. Vanilla combines it with `HouseAspiration.HasMultipleLevels` to show level parts of the window, and uses the negation of that pair to hide them.

label: Is selected level
summary: Whether the given level index is the selected one.
details: Vanilla passes the index of the level row and uses the result for the pressed state of the row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The index of the level to check.

label: Select aspiration
summary: Makes the given house aspiration the chosen one in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click and passes `HouseAspiration.Self`, the aspiration of the clicked entry. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The aspiration to choose.

label: The window itself
summary: The house aspiration window object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the window on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Select level
summary: Selects the level with the given index in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click and passes the index of the clicked level row. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The index of the level.

label: Show cooldown notice
summary: Whether the notice about the change cooldown should be shown.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the window. See `GetSelectedHouseAspirationCooldown` for the cooldown text.

label: Upgrade aspiration
summary: The command that upgrades the house's aspiration.
details: Vanilla checks it with `IsValidCommand` for the enabled state of a button, opens a confirmation popup with `CreateCommandPopup` on click, and shows the reason in the tooltip when it is not valid. It is a command, not a plain function.

label: Window itself (access)
summary: The house customization window object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Can click finish
summary: Whether the finish button can be clicked in the house customization window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the enabled state of a button. See `GetCanClickFinishText` for the matching tooltip.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the house customization window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click in the dynasty house customization GUI. It returns nothing.

label: Finish tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the finish button.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip. Going by its name, it explains whether or why finishing is possible. See `CanClickFinish`.

label: Coat of arms designer
summary: The coat of arms designer used in the house customization window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the part of the window where the house's coat of arms is edited. It returns a CoatOfArmsDesigner.

label: House
summary: The dynasty house being customized.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window, also with `.GetHeadOfHouse` for the house's head. The game documents no return type for it.

label: House name text
summary: The house name as currently typed in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of the name field. See `OnEditHouseNameText`.

label: Motto text
summary: The house motto as currently typed in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of the motto field. See `OnEditMottoText`.

label: Finish click
summary: Reacts to a click on the finish button of the house customization window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click. It returns nothing. Going by its name, it completes the customization.

label: House name edited
summary: Reacts when the house name field has been edited.
details: Vanilla runs it from the text-edited event of the name field. It returns nothing.

label: Motto edited
summary: Reacts when the motto field has been edited.
details: Vanilla runs it from the text-edited event of the motto field. It returns nothing.

label: The window itself
summary: The house customization window object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the window on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Option itself (access)
summary: The house order option object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Name
summary: The name of the house order option as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the dynasty house window. The same function name is used a very large number of times on other types.

label: The option itself
summary: The house order option object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the option on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Relation itself (access)
summary: The house relation object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Custom text
summary: A named custom text for the house relation.
details: Going by its name, it looks up a custom text by the given name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types (characters) use `.Custom('Name')` that way in texts, which is only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text.

label: Level progress tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about progress within the relation's current level.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the dynasty house window.

label: History
summary: The list of changes the house relation has gone through.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the history window and shows its size in texts. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Latest change amount
summary: How much the house relation changed the last time it changed, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets in faded text, with a plus or minus sign, as a percentage (the text `house_relation_latest_change_amount`). House relations are the standing between two dynasty houses.

label: Latest change date
summary: The date of the most recent change of the relation.
details: Vanilla writes it with `.GetString` in the house view's relation entry, after the description of the change. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Latest change description
summary: The text describing the most recent change of the relation.
details: Vanilla writes it in the house view's relation entry, before the date of the change. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Latest change if any
summary: Text about the house relation's latest change, shown after its description in the relation's messages.
details: Vanilla puts it right after the latest change's description in the messages that a house relation improved or was damaged. What it writes is not shown in the input; its name suggests it is empty when there was no change, which is a guess.

label: Level
summary: The current level of the house relation.
details: Vanilla asks the level for its name (`.GetName`) in the house view and in the texts of effects that change a house relation. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Level fraction
summary: A number for how far the relation has come within its current level.
details: Vanilla shows it with one decimal in the dynasty house window. That it is progress within the level is read from the name and the neighbouring tooltip function.

label: Name
summary: The name of the house relation as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the headings 'History of ...' of the house view and history window. The same function name is used a very large number of times on other types.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the house relation as plain text, without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as text in the dynasty house window and the history window. The no-tooltip part comes from the name.

label: Opposite house
summary: The house on the other side of the relation, seen from the given house.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. The dynasty house window uses the same name on a house relation item as a data context, which is only a hint. It takes one value, probably the house to look from.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A value the game does not describe; likely the house to look from.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the house relation.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the dynasty house window and the history window.

label: Relation type
summary: The type of the house relation.
details: Vanilla asks it for its levels (`.GetLevels`) as the data source of a list in the dynasty house window. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Index is relation change
summary: Whether the history entry with the given index is a change of the relation.
details: Vanilla passes the index of the history row and uses the result and its opposite to show different parts of the row. That it marks a change is read from the name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The index of the history entry.

label: Make scope
summary: The house relation as a script scope.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. Vanilla texts use `.MakeScope` on other types, for example the player, followed by a script value call (`ScriptValue('...')`), which is only a hint. It returns a Scope.

label: The relation itself
summary: The house relation object itself.
details: Vanilla passes it to another function: a click in the dynasty house window opens the history window for this relation.

label: Change itself (access)
summary: The house relation change object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Change amount
summary: How much the relation changed in this history entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as a signed percentage in the history window. It returns a fixed-point number.

label: Change date
summary: The date of this change of the relation.
details: Vanilla shows its text form in the history window. It returns a date.

label: Change description
summary: The text describing this change of the relation.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a history row in the history window.

label: Change level
summary: The relation level that belongs to this history entry.
details: Vanilla uses its rendered icon and its name in the history window. Whether it is the level before or after the change is not shown in the input. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Level tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the level of this history entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the history window.

label: Has non-zero amount
summary: Whether this change moved the relation, that is, its amount is not zero.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its opposite with `Not`, to show different parts of a history row.

label: The change itself
summary: The house relation change object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the change on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Window itself (access)
summary: The house relation history window object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the house relation history window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of two controls in the window. It returns nothing.

label: House relation
summary: The house relation whose history the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Left house
summary: The house shown on the left side of the history window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and also asks it for its head of house or last known head (`.GetHeadOfHouseOrLastHistoricHead`). The game documents no return type for it.

label: Right house
summary: The house shown on the right side of the history window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and also asks it for its head of house or last known head (`.GetHeadOfHouseOrLastHistoricHead`). The game documents no return type for it.

label: The window itself
summary: The house relation history window object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands the window on, for example as an argument. No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types use `.Self` that way, which is only a hint.

label: Item itself (access)
summary: The house relation list item object itself, handed on in the GUI.
details: Going by its name. No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same name on a widget is passed as an argument to a window function, which is only a hint.

label: Levels bar
summary: The bar that shows the levels of this house relation.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a bar in the dynasty house window. It returns a ComplexBar, a GUI bar object.

label: Name
summary: The name of the house relation item as text.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. The same function name is used a very large number of times on other types, which is only a hint.

label: Opinion
summary: The opinion number of the house relation item, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as text and compares it with numbers to show different parts for positive and negative opinion in the dynasty house window.

label: Opinion tint
summary: The text colour that goes with the opinion, as a four-part colour value.
details: Vanilla uses it as the font tint colour of the opinion text in the dynasty house window.
